title: 100 Objective Questions and Answers on Process Control Valves
queries: types of control loops in instrumentation
text:
Process Control Valves are used in industrial plants to regulate  flow ,  pressure ,  temperature , and  level  within a process system. 
 These valves are commonly found in refineries, power plants, chemical industries, water treatment facilities, and manufacturing units. For instrumentation students and working engineers, a clear understanding of process control valves is important for exams, interviews, and day-to-day field work. 
 This article presents 100 objective questions and answers on Process Control Valves , organised in batches of ten, with short explanations to help build strong fundamentals and practical clarity.
 
 
 Objective Questions on Process Control Valves (Q1–Q10) Q1. What is the main purpose of process control valves in an industrial system?
 a) Measure flow rate b) Regulate process variables c) Store process fluid d) Generate compressed air
 Correct Answer: b Explanation: Process control valves regulate variables such as flow, pressure, temperature, and level by adjusting the flow passage according to the control signal.
 Q2. Which process variable is most commonly controlled using control valves ?
 a) Density b) Flow c) Viscosity d) Conductivity
 Correct Answer: b Explanation: Flow control is the most common application of process control valves in industrial plants.
 Q3. Which signal is most widely used to control control valves in modern plants?
 a) 0–5 V b) 0–10 V c) 4–20 mA d) Pulse signal
 Correct Answer: c Explanation: A 4–20 mA signal is widely used due to its noise immunity and fault detection capability.
 Q4. Which component converts an electrical signal into valve movement in process control valves ?
 a) Valve body b) Actuator c) Bonnet d) Trim
 Correct Answer: b Explanation: The actuator converts the control signal (pneumatic, electric, or hydraulic) into mechanical motion to move the valve stem.
 Q5. What does “fail-safe position” mean in control valves ?
 a) Valve remains in last position b) Valve moves to a predefined safe position on failure c) Valve opens fully at high pressure d) Valve closes only during maintenance
 Correct Answer: b Explanation: In case of power or air failure, process control valves move to a predefined position to maintain process safety.
 Q6. Which type of actuator is most commonly used with control valves ?
 a) Manual actuator b) Electric actuator c) Pneumatic actuator d) Hydraulic actuator
 Correct Answer: c Explanation: Pneumatic actuators are widely used due to their simplicity, reliability, and suitability for hazardous areas.
 Q7. What is the function of a valve positioner in control valves ?
 a) Increase flow rate b) Control line pressure c) Ensure accurate valve positioning d) Reduce noise
 Correct Answer: c Explanation: A positioner ensures that the valve stem position accurately matches the control signal.
 Q8. Which part of  control valves directly throttles the flow?
 a) Actuator b) Bonnet c) Valve trim d) Yoke
 Correct Answer: c Explanation: The valve trim, including plug and seat, directly controls the amount of fluid passing through the valve.
 Q9. Which control action causes the valve to close when the control signal increases?
 a) Direct acting b) Reverse acting c) Fail-open d) Fail-close
 Correct Answer: b Explanation: In reverse-acting process control valves, an increase in signal causes the valve to close.
 Q10. Which parameter defines the flow capacity of control valves ?
 a) Valve size b) Pressure rating c) Cv value d) Actuator type
 Correct Answer: c Explanation: Cv represents the flow coefficient and indicates the flow capacity of process control valves under specified conditions
 Objective Questions on Process Control Valves (Q11–Q20) Q11. What does the term “valve trim” refer to in process control valves ?
 a) External coating of the valve b) Internal flow-controlling components c) Actuator mounting structure d) Valve body material
 Correct Answer: b Explanation: Valve trim includes internal parts such as the plug, seat, cage, and stem that control fluid flow in process control valves.
 Q12. Which type of control valve is most suitable for throttling applications?
 a) Gate valve b) Globe valve c) Check valve d) Plug valve
 Correct Answer: b Explanation: Globe valves provide good throttling characteristics and precise control, making them common in process control valves applications.
 Q13. What is the function of the valve bonnet in control valves ?
 a) Control flow rate b) House the actuator c) Seal the valve stem and connect body to actuator d) Reduce pressure drop
 Correct Answer: c Explanation: The bonnet provides a pressure boundary and contains the stem sealing arrangement in process control valves.
 Q14. Which valve characteristic provides a constant change in flow for a constant change in valve travel?
 a) Equal percentage b) Quick opening c) Linear d) Modified equal percentage
 Correct Answer: c Explanation: Linear characteristics provide a proportional relationship between valve travel and flow in process control valves.
 Q15. Which valve characteristic is preferred for wide range flow control in control valves ?
 a) Linear b) Quick opening c) Equal percentage d) On-off
 Correct Answer: c Explanation: Equal percentage characteristics are suitable for applications with large variations in flow demand.
 Q16. What happens when control valves operate under cavitation conditions?
 a) Valve flow increases b) Vapor bubbles form and collapse c) Valve closes automatically d) Pressure remains constant
 Correct Answer: b Explanation: Cavitation occurs when vapor bubbles form and collapse, causing noise, vibration, and damage to process control valves.
 Q17. Which factor has the greatest influence on sizing control valves ?
 a) Valve color b) Actuator brand c) Required flow rate and pressure drop d) Pipe insulation
 Correct Answer: c Explanation: Proper sizing of process control valves depends mainly on flow rate, pressure drop, and fluid properties.
